entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Construction of the Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility is entering its next phase, with critical components arriving and partner institutions contributing. UK groups have completed half of the 137 Anode Plane Assemblies, the sensors that detect the electrical signals produced when neutrinos interact in liquid argon. Black Hills State University has also become an institutional member, and the collaboration is described as more than 1,500 collaborators from 228 institutions in 38 countries and CERN.

entry.title: KM3NeT and gravitational waves
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT has announced a paper describing searches for coincident gravitational waves and high-energy neutrinos, using KM3NeT and ANTARES data from the O3 observing run. The motivation given is that sources of gravitational waves may also produce high-energy neutrinos. The collaboration also met in Siracusa for five days, with status updates on detector operations on the agenda.

entry.title: Project 8 dissociator
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Project 8 plans a model-independent neutrino mass measurement from tritium beta decay using cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy. A new paper describes a prototype electron cyclotron resonance dissociator that uses a 1 kW, 2.45 GHz RF generator and electromagnets to ignite a hydrogen plasma. The stated sensitivity goal for the final measurement is 40 meV/c^2.

entry.title: NINJA scintillator tracker
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A meter-scale scintillator tracker, FROST, was built and operated in the NINJA experiment to match muon tracks between the nuclear emulsion detectors and the downstream muon detector. During J-PARC neutrino-beam operation it reached a data acquisition efficiency of 99.59% and a detection efficiency of 99.946±0.006% for selected neutrino-induced muons well within the active area.

entry.title: Auger sterile neutrinos
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Pierre Auger Collaboration studied the observatory's sensitivity to sterile neutrinos of MeV-to-100 MeV mass, in a 3+1 framework where the sterile state mixes mainly with the tau flavour. Such neutrinos could cross long chords of the Earth and produce tau leptons that decay in the atmosphere and give detectable air showers. Exposures are computed with a Monte Carlo simulation of neutrino propagation.

entry.title: The paper examines neutrino emission from Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, which can accompany the nu
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper examines neutrino emission from Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, which can accompany the nucleonic Urca processes if Δ isobars are present in the dense core. The abstract states that the specific contribution of this process to neutrino emissivity had not been explicitly determined before. This is relevant to neutron-star cooling, where Urca processes are among the dominant mechanisms.

entry.title: The authors assess how kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could constrain the primary cosmic-ray
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors assess how kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could constrain the primary cosmic-ray spectrum through the atmospheric neutrino flux. They report that future detectors can distinguish between cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even allowing for uncertainties in cross sections and hadronic interactions. They also introduce a technique for reconstructing the primary spectrum.

entry.title: The paper gives semianalytic approximations for the outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion in quasihomoge
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper gives semianalytic approximations for the outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion in quasihomogeneous neutrino ensembles, as a subgrid scheme for hydrodynamic simulations that cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics. The ansatz agrees well with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations, independent of the mass ordering. It is useful for supernova modelling.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution that is covariant under r
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution that is covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is exactly blind to a Majorana phase in open two-flavour oscillations. A rate anisotropy in the environment can supply a phase reference, giving a dependence of the form A(t) + B(t) cos 2(ϕ − α). It therefore sets conditions for when decoherence could reveal a Majorana phase.

entry.title: Motivated by updated IceCube data for NGC 1068 down to about 0.2 TeV, the authors compute neutrino production
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Motivated by updated IceCube data for NGC 1068 down to about 0.2 TeV, the authors compute neutrino production from hadronic channels and the accompanying cascade gamma rays. They explore the parameter space with Latin hypercube sampling, constrained by multimessenger data. The abstract states that the emission region is tightly constrained, which bears on where neutrinos are made near the black hole.

entry.title: The paper investigates whether nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals could record neutrinos from past Gala
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper investigates whether nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals could record neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae. It varies neutron-star masses, includes failed supernovae that form black holes, and considers the role of the nuclear equation of state. The sensitivity is found to be enhanced for models with larger neutrino emission.
